## What you did

- Traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop to your own iOS SDK: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends `event_id` as a per-session counter, so the #240 dedupe discarded ~1.18M legitimate Orbitly events (8.1% of their iOS volume since 13/11), plus 3,812 for Zest's pilot app [1]
- Fixed the dedupe to key on (project, device, event_id) — genuine batch replays are still dropped — and opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer [1][2]

## What changed

- Maya will approve #247 once CI is green, but asked you for the number of Orbitly events dropped since #240, for her Thursday call with Orbitly [2]
- Noa's final version of the 12/11 postmortem is up; she presents it at Friday's incident review on 20/11 [3]
- The incident-review prep added an action item for you on the ingest dead-letter queue alert [7]

## What is still open

- Once #247 is merged and deployed, replay Orbitly from landing for 13/11 onward (~40 min, keeps the ~1.18M events and skips the 4,352 genuine replays), then the same for Zest, and check the dedupe drop counter stays near zero [1]
- Add the alert for the ingest dead-letter queue going above 1,000 messages, before Friday's review [7]
- The note asking the iOS team to restore UUIDs for `event_id` in kestrel-ios 3.2.1 is still a draft to send [1]
